name: Gnarly
blurb: Katseye's divisive 2025 hyperpop single whose dance break took over TikTok
title: Gnarly by Katseye: Why the Song Went Viral on TikTok
description: Gnarly is Katseye's 2025 hyperpop single. Its love-it-or-hate-it sound and sharp dance break made it a TikTok hit and their first Hot 100 entry.
h1: Why did "Gnarly" by Katseye go viral?
answer: "Gnarly" is a song by Katseye, the six-member global girl group formed by HYBE and Geffen Records, released on 30 April 2025 as the lead single of their EP Beautiful Chaos. Its chaotic hyperpop sound split listeners at first, and that debate, plus a sharp, angular dance break, flooded TikTok with reactions and dance covers. It became the group's first Billboard Hot 100 entry, peaking at No. 82.

body: The song is built from short shouted lines and a list of things called "gnarly", over a fast, glitchy beat. The viral part is the dance break: precise, angular arm and hand shapes in the style of tutting, hit hard on every beat. Fans post dance covers and tutorials, and the group's own dance-break clips drew millions of likes. Many early videos were simply people reacting to how strange it sounded.

body.note: Katseye are Daniela, Lara, Manon, Megan, Sophia and Yoonchae. They were chosen in the 2023 competition The Debut: Dream Academy, shown in the Netflix series Pop Star Academy: Katseye.

head: Date
Event
rows: An early demo of the song, from songwriter Alice Longyu Gao, surfaces on TikTok.
Katseye release "Gnarly"; reactions are sharply divided.
It spreads on TikTok and debuts at No. 92 on the Billboard Hot 100 (announced 13 May), the group's first entry.
The New York Times ranks it No. 2 on its best songs of 2025 list; NME puts it at No. 5.
It is nominated for Favorite TikTok Dance at the iHeartRadio Music Awards and wins Best Music Video at the American Music Awards (25 May).

body: "Gnarly" is American slang for something extreme, which can be extremely good or extremely gross. The members have said there are good gnarlies and bad gnarlies, and that the meaning is up to the listener. Songwriter Alice Longyu Gao said the idea came from noticing how Americans use one word to describe everything.

ul: Divisive sound: many people first called it the group's strangest song, and arguing about it became content in itself.
A dance break built for short videos: a few seconds of crisp, copyable moves.
A slow burn: the members say listeners do not "get" it on the first play, and it later landed on critics' year-end lists.
Chart peaks: No. 82 on the Hot 100, No. 41 on the Billboard Global 200 and No. 52 in the UK, the group's first entries in the US and UK.

faq.a: Katseye, a six-member girl group formed by HYBE and Geffen Records, whose members trained together in Los Angeles. The song was written by Alice Longyu Gao, Tim Randolph, Kyle Buckley, Jacob Kasher Hindlin and Madison Love.

faq.q: How do you do the "Gnarly" dance?
faq.a: The famous part is the dance break: sharp, boxy arm and hand shapes made in front of the body, each locked onto a beat, done with attitude. Most people learn it from mirrored tutorials of the group's dance practice.
Its shouty, chaotic hyperpop style is very different from usual girl-group pop, and the group has talked about the intense pushback. Plenty of listeners later said it grew on them.
